name: Masuda Tokubee Shoten
about: Masuda Tokubee Shoten began in 1675 beside the Toba Kaido road in Kyoto, running a sake shop and a rice shop. The brewery was damaged in the Battle of Toba-Fushimi in 1868 and rebuilt on its present site in Fushimi. The Tsuki no Katsura name comes from a poem by the courtier Ayanokoji Arinaga about drawing river water at night.
In 1964 the 13th head made a sparkling nigori sake that the brewery calls the first in Japan. Since 1965 it has aged junmai daiginjo in porcelain jars. It has also revived local sake rice.
